html:
Yaroslav the Wise was grand prince of Kyiv from 1019 to 1054, under whom Kyivan Rus reached its height of power, learning and contact with Europe.

A son of Volodymyr, who had made Rus Christian, he won a bloody fight for the throne with his brothers. He had the first written law code of Rus, the Russkaya Pravda, compiled. He built the Saint Sophia Cathedral and the Golden Gate in Kyiv, founded schools and libraries, and appointed the first native head of the Kyivan church. He married his daughters to the kings of France, Norway and Hungary, so that Anna of Kyiv became queen of France. After his death his sons divided the land, and Rus broke into rival principalities, later overrun in the Mongol invasion.
sum: Yaroslav the Wise was grand prince of Kyiv from 1019 to 1054, under whom Kyivan Rus reached its height of power, learning and contact with Europe.
